subject: Same precision parameters for multiple random effects

messages.author: 1a283d4938b39941
messages.subject: Same precision parameters for multiple random effects
parts:
Hello,

Is it possible to specify that two random effects use the same precision parameter in any way other than using 'replicate'? I'm interested in a model with several 'besag' terms that act on different variables, but I want them to share the same precision parameter. Without this constraint, the model would be specified like this:

outcome ~ s1 + s2 + s3 + f(dist1, s1, model="besag", graph=graph) + f(dist2, s2, model="besag", graph=graph) + f(dist3, s3, model="besag", graph=graph)

Thank you,
Laura

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Same precision parameters for multiple random effects
parts:
On 22 October 2012 16:35, Laura Dwyer-Lindgren
<laura.a...@gmail.com> > outcome ~ s1 + s2 + s3 + f(dist1, s1,

model="besag", graph=graph) + f(dist2,
> s2, model="besag", graph=graph) + f(dist3, s3, model="besag", graph=graph)

If the same graph is used for dist1, dist2 and dist3, then something
like this should do the trick:

dist.common = c(dist1,dist2,dist3),
s.common = c(s1,s2,s3)
replicate = c(rep(1,length(dist1)),rep(2,length(dist2)),rep(3,length(dist3)))

outcome ~ s1 + s2 + s3 + f(dist.common, s.common, model="besag",
replicate=replicate, graph=graph)

(If each dist* had its own graph this would not work.)

/Finn

> term, how can I make it apply to three different sets of variables?

ok, got it. its a bit unusual setting, but still doable.

to simplify the argument, assume we have to such models with graphs G1
and G2. conditional on the precision parameter, then they are
independent. so you can contruct a joint model, where the graph is G1
union G2. so for model1 you use the first n1 components, and for model2
you use the last n2 components. so either merge the two graphs, or use
the 'generic' model.

the only minor issue is that the rankdeficiency is 2, so you should use

f(..., rankdef = 2)

and not use constr=T. if you need that, you need to define this manually
with argument 'extraconstr' (ie two constraints).

H

messages.author: 1a283d4938b39941
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Same precision parameters for multiple random effects
parts: After further discussion with Havard and Finn, this seems to be the solution in my case where dist1, dist2, and dist3 are identical and share the same graph:
outcome ~ s1 + s2 + s3 +

f(dist1, s1, model="besag", graph=graph, replicate=rep(1,length(data$dist1)), nrep=3) +
     f(dist2, s2, replicate=rep(2,length(data$dist2)), copy="dist1") +
     f(dist3, s3, replicate=rep(3,length(data$dist3)), copy="dist1")
